sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%隐形”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In 1968, the police department in Menlo Park, California hired a new police chief.
sentences.zh: 1968年，加利福尼亚州门洛帕克的警察局雇用了一位新警察局长。

sentences.en: His name was Victor Cizankas.
sentences.zh: 他叫维克托·西赞卡斯。

sentences.en: And Chief Cizankas' main goal was to reform the police department's image,
sentences.zh: 西赞卡斯局长的主要目标是重塑警察局的形象，

sentences.en: which wasn't great at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时这个形象可不太好。

sentences.en: That's our own Delaney Hall.
sentences.zh: 那是我们的同事德兰尼·霍尔。

sentences.en: Because this was the 1960s, and even in Menlo Park,
sentences.zh: 因为那是20世纪60年代，即便是在门洛帕克，

sentences.en: a small city with manicured lawns and wide suburban streets,
sentences.zh: 这个拥有修剪整齐的草坪和宽阔郊区街道的小城市，

sentences.en: it had been a turbulent decade.
sentences.zh: 也是一个动荡的十年。

sentences.en: There were big, student-led anti-war demonstrations at Stanford University,
sentences.zh: 就在附近的斯坦福大学，爆发了由学生主导的大规模反战示威活动。

sentences.en: which is right nearby.
sentences.zh: 就在附近。

sentences.en: Joan Baez, the folk singer, created a commune called Struggle Mountain
sentences.zh: 民谣歌手琼·贝茨在城市上方的山麓建立了一个名为“斗争山”的公社。

sentences.en: in the foothills above the city.
sentences.zh: 在城市上方的山麓丘陵地带。

sentences.en: And leaders in the African-American community were organizing protests
sentences.zh: 非裔美国人社区的领袖们正在组织抗议活动，

sentences.en: to demand better treatment and services.
sentences.zh: 要求获得更好的对待和公共服务。

sentences.en: The Menlo Park police had clashed with these protesters, sometimes violently.
sentences.zh: 门洛帕克警方曾与这些抗议者发生冲突，有时甚至是暴力冲突。

sentences.en: And after years and years of this, the department had a pretty rough reputation.
sentences.zh: 年复一年之后，该警局的名声变得相当糟糕。

sentences.en: Had a reputation for being a very tough police department,
sentences.zh: 以作风极其强硬而闻名，

sentences.en: a very aggressive police department,
sentences.zh: 是一个极其激进的警察局，

sentences.en: and somewhat of a very anti-race kind of a police department.
sentences.zh: 而且多多少少带有很强的反少数族裔色彩。

sentences.en: That's Dominic Peloso.
sentences.zh: 那是多米尼克·佩洛索。

sentences.en: He was hired in 1970 by Chief Cizankas,
sentences.zh: 他在1970年被西赞卡斯局长招募，

sentences.en: the guy who wanted to change this culture.
sentences.zh: 也就是那个想要改变这种文化的人。

sentences.en: He was one of these type of guys that would come into a room
sentences.zh: 他属于那种一走进房间，

sentences.en: and would just fill in the room.
sentences.zh: 就能把整个房间填满的人。

sentences.en: You know, and everybody kind of sits back and says,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，大家都会往后一靠，心里想：

sentences.en: I think we better listen and go along with this guy.
sentences.zh: “我想我们最好还是听他的，顺着他来吧。”

sentences.en: Chief Cizankas had hired Dominic right out of the Jesuit seminary,
sentences.zh: 西赞卡斯局长刚把多米尼克从耶稣会神学院招安过来，

sentences.en: where Dominic had been studying to be a prieSt.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克当时正在那里学习成为一名神父。

sentences.en: Cizankas liked hiring officers from non-traditional law enforcement backgrounds
sentences.zh: 西赞卡斯喜欢从非传统执法背景、

sentences.en: and with higher levels of education.
sentences.zh: 且受过更高教育的人当中招募警员。

sentences.en: It was just one of his strategies for reforming the department.
sentences.zh: 这只是他重塑警局战略的一部分。

sentences.en: He also let his officers grow their hair out and have beards and mustaches.
sentences.zh: 他还允许警员留长发、蓄胡须和八字胡。

sentences.en: He changed all the pseudo-military titles to more corporate ones.
sentences.zh: 他把所有的准军事头衔换成了更具企业风格的称谓。

sentences.en: Sergeants became managers, for example,
sentences.zh: 例如，警长变成了经理，

sentences.en: and lieutenants became directors.
sentences.zh: 而中尉变成了总监。

sentences.en: Officers in the department had mixed feelings about all these changes,
sentences.zh: 警局里的警员对这些变化褒贬不一，

sentences.en: but one was more controversial than the others.
sentences.zh: 但其中一项比其他任何改革都更具争议。

sentences.en: For a long time, officers in Menlo Park had worn a variation
sentences.zh: 长期以来，门洛帕克的警察一直穿着一种改良版的

sentences.en: of the traditional dark blue police uniform.
sentences.zh: 传统深蓝色警服。

sentences.en: But Chief Cizankas thought that style was too intimidating and aggressive.
sentences.zh: 但西赞卡斯局长认为这种风格过于吓人且具有攻击性。

sentences.en: So the chief came up with something totally different.
sentences.zh: 于是局长想出了一个完全不同的方案。

sentences.en: It was really a nice, kind of a dark green blazer with some black thread in it.
sentences.zh: 那实际上是一件很好看的深绿色西装外套，里面带有黑色细线。

sentences.en: We wore pastel-colored solid shirts with a tie and slacks.
sentences.zh: 我们穿素色衬衫，系领带，配休闲裤。

sentences.en: Instead of a metal badge, the blazer sported an embroidered patch
sentences.zh: 西装外套上没有金属徽章，而是一个刺绣徽章，

sentences.en: that sort of looked like a coat of arMs.
sentences.zh: 看起来有点像家族徽章。

sentences.en: Guns and handcuffs remained hidden under the jacket.
sentences.zh: 枪支和手铐则藏在夹克底下。

sentences.en: All in all, the officers looked kind of like grown-up prep school students,
sentences.zh: 总而言之，警员们看起来有点像成年版的预科学校学生，

sentences.en: but with guns.
sentences.zh: 只不过带着枪。

sentences.en: They even had pocket protectors with the Menlo Park Police logo on it
sentences.zh: 他们的正装衬衫口袋里甚至插着印有门洛帕克警察局标志的口袋保护套。

sentences.en: that would slide into the pocket of their dress shirts.
sentences.zh: 正好能塞进他们正装衬衫的口袋里。

sentences.en: It seems like the total effect is he was trying to demilitarize
sentences.zh: 这给人的总体感觉似乎是，他正试图去军事化

sentences.en: the look and attitude of the department.
sentences.zh: 警局的外观和态度。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that would be a correct statement.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这种说法是准确的。

sentences.en: A lot of the guys who join police departments are from the military,
sentences.zh: 很多加入警察局的人都曾从军，

sentences.en: and because of the nature of the work, it can be very militaristic,
sentences.zh: 由于工作性质的原因，它可能会非常军事化，

sentences.en: shall we say, in organization and training and all those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 可以说，在组织、训练以及所有这些方面都是如此。

sentences.en: And he was trying to calm it down.
sentences.zh: 而他当时正试图缓和这种氛围。

sentences.en: But Chief Cizankas was also messing with a tradition
sentences.zh: 但西赞卡斯局长同时也触动了一个传统，

sentences.en: that would prove extremely hard to change.
sentences.zh: 事实证明这个传统极其难以改变。

sentences.en: Because the blue military-style uniform
sentences.zh: 因为这种蓝色的军用风格制服

sentences.en: had a history that went back more than 100 years.
sentences.zh: 有着一百多年的历史。

sentences.en: What we've asked police officers to wear over the years
sentences.zh: 多年来我们要求警察穿什么服装，

sentences.en: says a lot about what we've expected of them
sentences.zh: 很大程度上说明了我们对他们的期望，

sentences.en: and how we feel about them.
sentences.zh: 以及我们对他们的看法。

sentences.en: It even says a lot about how they feel about themselves.
sentences.zh: 甚至很大程度上说明了他们对自己的看法。

sentences.en: Back in America's colonial days,
sentences.zh: 回溯到美国的殖民地时期，

sentences.en: law enforcement looked really different than it does now.
sentences.zh: 执法方式与现在截然不同。

sentences.en: In New England, there were these informal groups,
sentences.zh: 在新英格兰，有一些非正式的群体，

sentences.en: generally known as the Watch,
sentences.zh: 通常被称为“守夜队”，

sentences.en: that patrolled neighborhoods looking for crime.
sentences.zh: 他们在街区巡逻以寻找犯罪迹象。

sentences.en: No uniforms, no sort of organizational policies that they had to follow.
sentences.zh: 没有制服，也没有必须遵守的组织政策。

sentences.en: It was basically every able man.
sentences.zh: 基本上所有身强力壮的男子都要参与。

sentences.en: Chad Posick teaches in the Department of Criminal Justice and Criminology
sentences.zh: 查德·波西克在佐治亚南方大学的刑事司法与犯罪学系任教。

sentences.en: at Georgia Southern University.
sentences.zh: 在佐治亚南方大学。

sentences.en: If they saw somebody that needed help, a fire, crime on the corner,
sentences.zh: 如果他们看到有人需要帮助、发生火灾或街角有犯罪活动，

sentences.en: it would just be an informal group that would sort of respond to that.
sentences.zh: 就会有一个非正式的群体去做出响应。

sentences.en: So that was in the North.
sentences.zh: 所以那是北方的形式。

sentences.en: In Southern communities leading up to the Civil War,
sentences.zh: 而在南北战争前的南方社区，

sentences.en: there were roving patrols that were responsible for suppressing slave revolts
sentences.zh: 有专门负责镇压奴隶起义和搜捕逃亡奴隶的巡逻队。

sentences.en: and tracking down runaway slaves.
sentences.zh: 并搜捕逃跑的奴隶。

sentences.en: They worked for large plantation owners.
sentences.zh: 他们为大型种植园主工作。

sentences.en: So very much in the South, early policing was tied to slavery,
sentences.zh: 所以在南方，早期的执法活动与奴隶制紧密相连，

sentences.en: where in the North, it was more police and crime in these large urban areas.
sentences.zh: 而在北方，则更多涉及这些大型城区的治安和犯罪。

sentences.en: These unofficial patrols were how early law enforcement worked for decades.
sentences.zh: 这些非官方的巡逻队就是早期执法运作了几十年的方式。

sentences.en: It wasn't until the 1820s that modern policing began to take shape.
sentences.zh: 直到19世纪20年代，现代警务才开始成型。

sentences.en: Thanks to a British statesman named Sir Robert Peel.
sentences.zh: 这要归功于一位名叫罗伯特·皮尔的英国政治家。

sentences.en: Before Peel came along, policing in London looked a lot like it did in colonial America,
sentences.zh: 在皮尔出现之前，伦敦的警务看起来很像殖民地时期的美国，

sentences.en: informal and loosely organized.
sentences.zh: 非正式且组织松散。

sentences.en: And Peel recognized that there were problems with this model.
sentences.zh: 皮尔意识到这种模式存在问题。

sentences.en: People not taking it seriously, being drunk on the job, not showing up, falling asleep.
sentences.zh: 人们不把它当回事、在岗喝酒、缺勤、上班睡觉。

sentences.en: And so what he wanted to do is create a police department that was based on certain principles.
sentences.zh: 因此他想做的是建立一个基于某些原则的警察局。

sentences.en: And after years of pushing for reform, Peel succeeded.
sentences.zh: 经过多年的改革推动，皮尔成功了。

sentences.en: In 1829, he helped found the London Metropolitan Police,
sentences.zh: 1829年，他协助创立了伦敦大都会警察局，

sentences.en: the first modern, full-time, citywide police department.
sentences.zh: 这是第一个现代的、专职的、全市范围的警察局。

sentences.en: British officers are still known as Bobbies in honor of Robert Bobby Peel.
sentences.zh: 为了纪念罗伯特·“鲍比”·皮尔，英国警察至今仍被称为“鲍比”（Bobbies）。

sentences.en: In Ireland, they called them Peelers with a little less affection.
sentences.zh: 在爱尔兰，人们称他们为“皮尔斯”（Peelers），语气没那么亲切。

sentences.en: Peel required his officers to wear uniforms that would distinguish them from citizens they were meant to serve.
sentences.zh: 皮尔要求他的警员穿着能够将他们与他们所服务的公民区分开来的制服。

sentences.en: But Peel was also sensitive to how British people might perceive this new police force.
sentences.zh: 但皮尔也很在意英国民众会如何看待这支新警察部队。

sentences.en: Yes, that was a huge concern.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个巨大的担忧。

sentences.en: Because for so many years, the people were ruled by the military in a military state.
sentences.zh: 因为多年来，人们一直受到军政府在军事状态下的统治。

sentences.en: Peel wanted the new police uniforms to stand apart from the red coats of the British military.
sentences.zh: 皮尔希望新警察的制服能与英国军队的红制服区分开来。

sentences.en: That's sort of where we get our first blue uniform that was very professional looking.
sentences.zh: 这也就是我们获得第一套看起来非常专业的蓝色制服的由来。

sentences.en: And it actually stood in stark contrast to the red that you saw with the military.
sentences.zh: 它实际上与你在军队中看到的红色形成了鲜明对比。

sentences.en: Gradually, Peel's ideas and his blue uniform made their way to the United States.
sentences.zh: 渐渐地，皮尔的理念和他的蓝色制服传到了美国。

sentences.en: By the early 1900s, police departments across the country had adopted aspects of the style and approach
sentences.zh: 到20世纪初，全国各地的警察局都采用了由伦敦大都会警察局首创的

sentences.en: pioneered by the London Metropolitan Police.
sentences.zh: 这种风格和方法的某些方面。

sentences.en: This included a quasi-military structure and the goal of crime prevention.
sentences.zh: 这包括准军事结构以及预防犯罪的目标。

sentences.en: But there were still some probleMs.
sentences.zh: 但仍然存在一些问题。

sentences.en: Most early police departments in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国早期的绝大多数警察局

sentences.en: allied themselves with the rich and the powerful,
sentences.zh: 都与富人和权贵结盟，

sentences.en: like local politicians and business leaders.
sentences.zh: 比如地方政客和商业领袖。

sentences.en: And you might be thinking, it's still like that now.
sentences.zh: 你可能会想，现在不还是这样吗。

sentences.en: And you might be right.
sentences.zh: 你说得也许没错。

sentences.en: But it was worse then.
sentences.zh: 但那时情况更糟。

sentences.en: Like a new mayor would get elected and then would appoint a hand-picked police chief.
sentences.zh: 比如新市长当选后，就会任命一位自己精心挑选的警察局长。

sentences.en: Then the police chief would hire their family, their friends, to become the officers of that department.
sentences.zh: 然后警察局长会雇用自己的家人和朋友来担任该局的警员。

sentences.en: So very political.
sentences.zh: 所以非常具有政治色彩。

sentences.en: And obviously, if you're the police chief and you sort of work for the mayor, the local politician,
sentences.zh: 显然，如果你是警察局长，而且你某种程度上受雇于市长和地方政客，

sentences.en: you're going to serve their purposes first and the community maybe secondarily.
sentences.zh: 你就会首先服务于他们的目的，而社区则退居其次。

sentences.en: It was a patronage system.
sentences.zh: 这是一个政客分肥制系统。

sentences.en: And in most departments, recruits didn't receive any special training.
sentences.zh: 在大多数警局里，新兵收不到任何专门的训练。

sentences.en: They were just handed a badge and a nightstick and sent out on patrol.
sentences.zh: 他们只是被发给一个徽章和一根警棍，就被派去巡逻了。

sentences.en: Despite the spiffy new uniforms and their newly organized approach,
sentences.zh: 尽管有漂亮的全新制服和新组织的运作方式，

sentences.en: public trust in the police was dismal.
sentences.zh: 公众对警察的信任度仍然低谷盘旋。

sentences.en: So a reform movement begins to grow across America.
sentences.zh: 于是，一场改革运动开始在美国各地蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: And then in 1929, President Herbert Hoover convenes a group called the Wickersham Commission
sentences.zh: 接着在1929年，赫伯特·胡佛总统召集了一个名为“威克斯汉姆委员会”的组织，

sentences.en: to conduct the first national study of the American criminal justice system.
sentences.zh: 对美国刑事司法系统进行了首次全国性研究。

sentences.en: And they basically saw the infiltration of politics into policing as a huge problem.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上认为政治对警务的渗透是一个巨大问题。

sentences.en: And they said that we need to change up how we do things.
sentences.zh: 他们表示我们需要改变办事方式。

sentences.en: The Wickersham report shocked the country by exposing widespread police abuse.
sentences.zh: 威克斯汉姆报告揭露了普遍存在的警察滥用职权现象，震惊了全国。

sentences.en: It described police routinely beating suspects and holding them illegally for lengthy questioning.
sentences.zh: 其中描述了警察常规性地殴打嫌疑人，并将其非法拘禁进行长时间审讯。

sentences.en: And you might be thinking, it's still like that now.
sentences.zh: 你可能会想，现在不还是这样吗。

sentences.en: And you might be right.
sentences.zh: 你说得也许没错。

sentences.en: But it was worse then.
sentences.zh: 但那时情况更糟。

sentences.en: The report included some pretty disturbing accounts,
sentences.zh: 该报告包含了一些相当令人不安的记录，

sentences.en: like a suspect who was held by the ankles from a third-story window
sentences.zh: 比如一名嫌疑人被倒吊在三楼窗户外，脚踝悬空，

sentences.en: and another who was forced to stand in the morgue with his hands on the body of a murder victim.
sentences.zh: 还有另一名嫌疑人被强迫站在停尸房里，双手按在一名谋杀受害者的尸体上。

sentences.en: This report, the Wickersham report, really was sort of this turning point
sentences.zh: 这份报告，即威克斯汉姆报告，确实成为了这样一个转折点：

sentences.en: and we need to do something different in policing.
sentences.zh: 我们必须在警务工作上采取不同的做法。

sentences.en: And I think that's what led into this professional era.
sentences.zh: 我认为正是这一点引领我们进入了职业化时代。

sentences.en: This new professional era, which continued up into the 1960s and 70s,
sentences.zh: 这个新的职业化时代一直持续到20世纪60和70年代，

sentences.en: was characterized by an emphasis on policing as a skilled profession.
sentences.zh: 其特点是强调警务是一门熟练的专业。

sentences.en: This old educational film called Your Police lays it out.
sentences.zh: 这部名为《你的警察》的古老教育片对此作了阐述。

sentences.en: Police departments use modern science to protect you, such as teletype, photography,
sentences.zh: 警察局利用现代科学来保护你，例如电传打字机、摄影、

sentences.en: two-way radio, expert firearms training as standardized by the FBI National Academy, accident prevention installations and other...
sentences.zh: 双向无线电、由联邦调查局国家学院标准化的专家级枪械训练、事故预防设施以及其他……

sentences.en: Now police were trained to use modern tools and technology.
sentences.zh: 现在，警察接受了使用现代工具和技术的培训。

sentences.en: And one of the leading voices for this new method was a guy named August Vollmer.
sentences.zh: 而这一新方法的主导声音之一是一个名叫奥古斯特·沃尔默的人。

sentences.en: He'd been the first police chief of Berkeley, California, and he helped to write the Wickersham report.
sentences.zh: 他是加利福尼亚州伯克利的第一任警察局长，并协助撰写了威克斯汉姆报告。

sentences.en: Vollmer got his officers to use motorcycles and patrol cars instead of just walking around.
sentences.zh: 沃尔默让他的警官们骑摩托车和开巡逻车，而不是只在街上步行巡逻。

sentences.en: That way they could cover bigger areas more efficiently.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就能更高效地覆盖更大的区域。

sentences.en: He was also one of the first chiefs in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他也是美国最早的几位警察局长之一，

sentences.en: to insist his department use fingerprinting and blood and fiber analysis to help solve crimes.
sentences.zh: 坚持让他的部门使用指纹识别、血液和纤维分析来协助破案。

sentences.en: And under his influence, California became a hotbed of police reform from the 1920s through the 1960s,
sentences.zh: 在他的影响下，加利福尼亚州从20世纪20年代到60年代成了警务改革的温床，

sentences.en: leading, of course, to stuff like Chief Sizankis' blazer uniform experiment in Menlo Park.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也直接促成了诸如门洛帕克市西赞卡斯局长的西装外套制服实验之类的事情。

sentences.en: For a few years, it seemed like Chief Sizankis' reforms might be working.
sentences.zh: 有那么几年，西赞卡斯局长的改革似乎起作用了。

sentences.en: In blazers and ties and pocket protectors, the Menlo Park police definitely looked less intimidating.
sentences.zh: 穿着西装外套、系着领带、插着口袋保护套，门洛帕克警察看起来确实没那么吓人了。

sentences.en: Here's Dominic Peloso again.
sentences.zh: 这位再次登场的是多米尼克·佩洛索。

sentences.en: He eventually became assistant chief under Sizankis.
sentences.zh: 他后来成了西赞卡斯手下的副局长。

sentences.en: It wasn't like we slacked off and became, you know, like,
sentences.zh: 并不是说我们就此懈怠了，变成那种，你知道的，

sentences.en: oh, mercy and forgiveness and love and peace and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 哦，满怀仁慈、宽恕、爱与和平以及诸如此类的情绪。

sentences.en: You know, oh, no.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，哦，才没有。

sentences.en: But the way we did it and the style that we gave to people, I think,
sentences.zh: 但我们做事的方式以及我们展现给人们的风貌，我认为，

sentences.en: made them feel a lot better about us.
sentences.zh: 让他们对我们的感觉好多了。

sentences.en: And he built up a lot of really good rapport with the community.
sentences.zh: 他与社区建立了非常良好的关系。

sentences.en: There was even an early study suggesting that altercations between citizens and the police had declined because of the blazers.
sentences.zh: 甚至有一项早期研究表明，由于穿了西装外套，市民与警察之间的冲突减少了。

sentences.en: The study was later challenged, but when it first came out,
sentences.zh: 这项研究后来受到质疑，但在它刚问世时，

sentences.en: word began to spread and a few other departments across the country adopted the blazer style.
sentences.zh: 消息开始传开，全国其他几个部门也采用了西装外套的风格。

sentences.en: But the uniform experiment also drew a line within the department.
sentences.zh: 但制服实验也在警局内部划出了一条界线。

sentences.en: There were the guys, like Dominic, who liked what the blazers stood for.
sentences.zh: 有一群像多米尼克这样的人，他们喜欢西装外套所代表的理念。

sentences.en: They embraced that Chief Sizankis wanted the department to have a calmer, more professional image.
sentences.zh: 他们赞同西赞卡斯局长希望警局呈现出一种更平静、更专业的形象。

sentences.en: There's a lot of guys who want to do this job, but don't want to go out there and knock heads or shoot people or,
sentences.zh: 有很多人想做这份工作，但又不想去跟人硬碰硬、开枪打人或者，

sentences.en: you know, whatever like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: They just want to do the best for the community.
sentences.zh: 他们只想为社区尽最大努力。

sentences.en: And I think with our uniform, people who were applying got more of the sense that we really were community-minded,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为有了我们的制服，前来应聘的人会更强烈地感觉到我们确实是以社区为本、

sentences.en: helping people.
sentences.zh: 热心助人的。

sentences.en: On the other side were the old school police officers, who missed the traditional uniform and all that it represented.
sentences.zh: 另一边则是老派警察，他们怀念传统制服及其代表的一切。

sentences.en: They enjoyed the ego stuff that goes with it.
sentences.zh: 他们享受随之而来的自我优越感。

sentences.en: They also enjoy that sense of authority that you show, the clearness of who they are.
sentences.zh: 他们也享受那种你所展现出的权威感，以及他们身份的清晰度。

sentences.en: With the blazer, it just wasn't always that clear.
sentences.zh: 而穿了西装外套，这种身份就不总是那么清晰了。

sentences.en: You know, I'd stop a person, let's say, for a violation, and I'd walk up and say,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比方说我拦下一个人，因为他们违章了，然后我走过去说，

sentences.en: can I see your license, you know?
sentences.zh: 我能看一下你的驾照吗，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And they'd look at you and say, well, let's see your license.
sentences.zh: 他们会看着你说，好吧，那我也看看你的驾照。

sentences.en: You know, who are you?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你是谁啊？

sentences.en: Then you'd point to the pillow patch and say, well, I'm the police, you know.
sentences.zh: 然后你得指着徽章说，好吧，我是警察，你知道的。

sentences.en: This is retired Sergeant Van Trask.
sentences.zh: 这位是退休警长范·特拉斯克。

sentences.en: He worked under Sazankas, and generally he liked the chief's style and approach.
sentences.zh: 他在萨赞卡斯手下工作过，总的来说他很喜欢局长的风格和方法。

sentences.en: But he admits that it caused some complications.
sentences.zh: 但他承认这确实带来了一些麻烦。

sentences.en: You didn't have that much recognition as a cop, so you kind of, there's a tendency to get more,
sentences.zh: 你作为警察的辨识度没那么高，所以你就会有一种倾向，变得更倾向于，

sentences.en: who are you, you know, hey, I'm the police, you know, sure you are.
sentences.zh: 你是谁啊，你知道的，嘿，我是警察，你知道的，是吗，你当然是。

sentences.en: Many officers got so frustrated that they quit.
sentences.zh: 许多警官感到如此沮丧以至于辞职了。

sentences.en: The numbers we've heard on this vary.
sentences.zh: 我们听到的关于这方面的数据各不相同。

sentences.en: Van said about half the department left.
sentences.zh: 范说大约有一半的警局人员离职了。

sentences.en: Dominic thinks it was even higher.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克认为比例甚至更高。

sentences.en: I would guess that in his first four years as police chief, we had about a 75% turnover.
sentences.zh: 我估计在他担任警察局长的头四年里，我们的员工流动率达到了大约75%。

sentences.en: People just left and went to other departments.
sentences.zh: 人们纷纷离职并去了其他部门。

sentences.en: But I think they just couldn't take his overall thinking, his out-of-the-box thinking, his philosophy and stuff.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们只是无法接受他的总体思维、他的创新思维、他的哲学之类的那套东西。

sentences.en: So they all just abandoned.
sentences.zh: 所以他们全都放弃了。

sentences.en: And eventually Sazankas left, too, to take over as the chief of a police department in Stamford, Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 最终萨赞卡斯也离开了，去接任康涅狄格州斯坦福市警察局的局长。

sentences.en: You know, there's some talk that he was actually kind of encouraged to leave.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有传言称他其实是被变相鼓励离开的。

sentences.en: And not long after he left, the department switched back to the traditional uniform style.
sentences.zh: 就在他离开后不久，警局又换回了传统的制服风格。

sentences.en: Sazankas passed away in 1980.
sentences.zh: 萨赞卡斯于1980年逝世。

sentences.en: The year that Sazankas joined the Menlo Park Police Department, 1968,
sentences.zh: 萨赞卡斯加入门洛帕克警察局的那一年，即1968年，

sentences.en: represented an important turning point for law enforcement in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 是美国执法部门的一个重要转折点。

sentences.en: The community policing approach championed by Sazankas would continue to gain traction through the 80s and 90s,
sentences.zh: 萨赞卡斯倡导的社区警务方法在80和90年代继续获得广泛认可，

sentences.en: as departments across the country tried to build better, less combative relationships with their local communities.
sentences.zh: 因为全国各地的警局都在努力与当地社区建立更好、冲突更少的关系。

sentences.en: But there had always been a tension between the more community-oriented side of policing and the more military side.
sentences.zh: 但偏向社区一侧的警务与偏向军事一侧的警务之间一直存在着一种紧张关系。

sentences.en: And that was about to intensify.
sentences.zh: 而这种紧张即将加剧。

sentences.en: In recent years, crime in this country has grown nine times as fast as population.
sentences.zh: 近年来，这个国家的犯罪率增长速度是人口增长速度的九倍。

sentences.en: At the current rate, the crimes of violence in America will double by 1972.
sentences.zh: 按目前的速度，美国的暴力犯罪到1972年将翻一番。

sentences.en: We cannot accept that kind of future for America.
sentences.zh: 我们不能接受美国拥有那样的一个未来。

sentences.en: In 1968, Richard Nixon ran for president on a promise of law and order.
sentences.zh: 1968年，理查德·尼克松以法律与秩序的承诺竞选总统。

sentences.en: He tapped into all the paranoia and unease that had grown during the turmoil of the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 他利用了在20世纪60年代的动荡中滋生的所有偏执与不安。

sentences.en: His campaign ads were full of these scary images of urban unrest and rioting.
sentences.zh: 他的竞选广告里充满了城市动乱和暴乱的可怕画面。

sentences.en: And they ended with his slogan written across the screen.
sentences.zh: 最后以他的标语横贯屏幕作为结束。

sentences.en: Vote like your whole world depended on it.
sentences.zh: 投票吧，就像你的整个世界都维系于此一样。

sentences.en: I pledge to you, the wave of crime is not going to be the wave of the future in America.
sentences.zh: 我向你们保证，犯罪浪潮不会成为美国未来的浪潮。

sentences.en: Shortly after taking office, Nixon vowed to fight the war on crime, which had been started by his predecessor, Lyndon Johnson.
sentences.zh: 上任后不久，尼克松誓言要打击由其前任林登·约翰逊发起的打击犯罪战争。

sentences.en: He also declared a war on drugs.
sentences.zh: 他还宣佈了向毒品宣战。

sentences.en: Again, criminal justice professor Chad Posick.
sentences.zh: 再次有请刑事司法教授查德·波西克。

sentences.en: One, I think the language is very important, right?
sentences.zh: 第一，我认为这种用词非常重要，对吧？

sentences.en: You don't have, say, drug prevention or crime prevention.
sentences.zh: 你用的不是什么毒品预防或犯罪预防。

sentences.en: It's the war.
sentences.zh: 而是战争。

sentences.en: War on drugs.
sentences.zh: 禁毒战争。

sentences.en: The war on crime.
sentences.zh: 打击犯罪战争。

sentences.en: So you do see an escalation during this time on how crime is responded to.
sentences.zh: 所以你确实会发现在这段时间里，应对犯罪的方式升级了。

sentences.en: And it's responded to like they're responding to war.
sentences.zh: 人们对待犯罪的方式就像是在对待战争一样。

sentences.en: War, of course, requires specialized equipment.
sentences.zh: 当然，战争需要专门的装备。

sentences.en: And around this same time, the government established the Law Enforcement Assistance Administration,
sentences.zh: 大约在同一时期，政府成立了执法援助署，

sentences.en: a now-defunct federal agency that gave lots of money to local police departments
sentences.zh: 这是一个现已废止的联邦机构，它向地方警察部门提供大量资金，

sentences.en: so they could buy new-fangled crime-fighting tools.
sentences.zh: 以便他们能够购买新奇的打击犯罪工具。

sentences.en: You see this uptick in support for all sorts of policing, but especially riot gear and SWAT teams
sentences.zh: 你可以看到各方对所有类型的警务支持都在激增，尤其是防暴装备、特警队、

sentences.en: and armored vehicles and weapons and bulletproof vests and those types of things.
sentences.zh: 装甲车、武器、防弹衣以及诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: Even small rural departments were getting their hands on stuff like helicopters
sentences.zh: 就连小型农村警局也能弄到直升机之类的新鲜玩艺，

sentences.en: and serious crowd-control gear like shields and helmets.
sentences.zh: 以及盾牌和头盔等严肃的控场装备。

sentences.en: And new paramilitary divisions of the police, like SWAT teams, began using this gear.
sentences.zh: 警察部门的新准军事部队，如特警队，开始使用这些装备。

sentences.en: Some exchanged the traditional blue uniform for camouflage outfits, known as the battle dress uniform.
sentences.zh: 一些人将传统的蓝色制服换成了被称为作战服的迷彩服。

sentences.en: They began to look more military.
sentences.zh: 他们开始看起来更像军队了。

sentences.en: As this kind of equipment and style spread, so did more militarized policing tactics.
sentences.zh: 随着这种装备和风格的蔓延，更加军事化的警务战术也随之蔓延。

sentences.en: Conducting raids, crackdowns, and partially enforcing laws.
sentences.zh: 开展突袭、严厉打击，并有选择地执法。

sentences.en: They're behind the mask that they wear in riot gear or the big, huge vest that they wear in the SWAT team.
sentences.zh: 他们躲在防暴装备的面具后面，或者躲在特警队那身笨重硕大的防弹衣后面。

sentences.en: This trend continued through the 80s and 90s in lots of police departments across the country.
sentences.zh: 这一趋势在80和90年代延续到了全国各地的许多警察局。

sentences.en: It accelerated in many places after 9-11, as police departments became closer with federal law enforcement agencies
sentences.zh: 9·11事件后，许多地方的这一趋势加速了，当时警察局与联邦执法机构的关系更加密切，

sentences.en: and started thinking of themselves as part of the first line of defense in a new war, the War on Terror.
sentences.zh: 并开始认为自己是一场新战争——反恐战争——的第一道防线的一部分。

sentences.en: New federal programs emerged that sent surplus military equipment from Iraq and Afghanistan
sentences.zh: 新的联邦项目涌现出来，将来自伊拉克和阿富汗的剩余军事装备运送到

sentences.en: to local police departments across the country.
sentences.zh: 全国各地的地方警察局。

sentences.en: Which brings us to today.
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带到了今天。

sentences.en: I'm agitated because the police just arrested someone.
sentences.zh: 我很激动，因为警察刚刚逮捕了某个人。

sentences.en: They're basically confronting the police, yelling at them over this arreSt.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是在与警察对峙，为这次逮捕朝警察大喊大叫。

sentences.en: Back up, please!
sentences.zh: 请往后退！

sentences.en: Across the country, there have been highly publicized protests against police shootings of unarmed black men, women, and even children.
sentences.zh: 在全国范围内，爆发了针对警察枪杀未武装的黑人男性、女性甚至儿童的高调抗议活动。

sentences.en: And these protests have sparked bigger conversations about police violence and also how our police look.
sentences.zh: 这些抗议活动引发了关于警察暴力以及我们警察外表的更大规模讨论。

sentences.en: For several nights this week, this was Ferguson, Missouri.
sentences.zh: 在这一周的几个夜晚里，这就是密苏里州的弗格森。

sentences.en: Tanks, combat gear, assault rifles.
sentences.zh: 坦克、作战装备、突击步枪。

sentences.en: It looked like a military operation.
sentences.zh: 这看起来像是一场军事行动。

sentences.en: And that's because police departments...
sentences.zh: 那是因为警察部门……

sentences.en: The current mistrust of police seems to mirror what was going on in Menlo Park back in 1968, pre-Blazer, but on a more dramatic scale.
sentences.zh: 目前对警察的不信任似乎反映了1968年门洛帕克（穿西装外套之前）发生的事情，但规模更加戏剧化。

sentences.en: Back in the 1960s, it was big conversations about the role of police and the community that led Chief Sizankas to make changes to the Menlo Park uniform.
sentences.zh: 早在20世纪60年代，正是关于警察在社区中角色的重大讨论，促使西赞卡斯局长改变了门洛帕克的警服。

sentences.en: Today, at least so far, no departments have taken steps that drastic.
sentences.zh: 今天，至少到目前为止，还没有哪个部门采取如此激进的措施。

sentences.en: But in Minneapolis, they're taking a small step in that general direction.
sentences.zh: 但在明尼阿波利斯，他们正朝着那个大致方向迈出一小步。

sentences.en: Minneapolis SWAT teens will soon unveil a new look to make them appear less intimidating.
sentences.zh: 明尼阿波利斯特警队不久将展示一种新外观，使他们看起来不那么吓人。

sentences.en: In February of 2016, the Minneapolis Police Department changed the color of their SWAT uniforms from a military green to a more traditional navy blue.
sentences.zh: 2016年2月，明尼阿波利斯警察局将特警制服的颜色从军绿色改成了更传统的藏青色。

sentences.en: This happened about four months after the city saw widespread protests, after the police shot and killed an unarmed black man named Jamar Clark.
sentences.zh: 这发生在密歇根州（注：此处应为明尼苏达州，按原文翻译即可：在这座城市爆发广泛抗议活动大约四个月后，此前警察开枪打死了一名叫贾马尔·克拉克的未武装黑人男子）。

sentences.en: The Minneapolis Police Department declined to talk with us about the uniform change,
sentences.zh: 明尼阿波利斯警察局拒绝就制服更换一事接受我们的采访，

sentences.en: but they've made it clear in other interviews that this color change is about public perception and rebranding.
sentences.zh: 但他们在其他采访中明确表示，这种颜色改变关乎公众感知和品牌重塑。

sentences.en: We are police.
sentences.zh: 我们是警察。

sentences.en: We are not military.
sentences.zh: 我们不是军队。

sentences.en: We don't train with the military.
sentences.zh: 我们不随同军队一起训练。

sentences.en: We're not associated with the military.
sentences.zh: 我们与军队没有任何关联。

sentences.en: We're the Minneapolis Police Department, and we want to be reflective of our own community and our own image.
sentences.zh: 我们是明尼阿波利斯警察局，我们希望反映出我们自己的社区和我们自己的形象。

sentences.en: What's not totally clear is if the color of the uniform actually matters.
sentences.zh: 完全不清楚的是制服的颜色是否真的重要。

sentences.en: I mean, they can wear pink, but if they're toting guns and rubber bullets and mace and tasers and everything else.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们可以穿粉红色，但如果他们携带枪支、橡胶子弹、梅斯毒气、泰瑟枪以及其他所有东西。

sentences.en: This is Candace Montgomery.
sentences.zh: 这位是坎迪斯·蒙哥马利。

sentences.en: She's an activist with Black Lives Matter, and she's taken part in protests in Minneapolis against the police.
sentences.zh: 她是“黑人的命也是命”运动的一名活动人士，曾参加过明尼阿波利斯反对警察的抗议活动。

sentences.en: A color is not going to change that dynamic.
sentences.zh: 一种颜色并不能改变这种动态。

sentences.en: An entire overhaul of the policing system is going to change that dynamic in people's responses.
sentences.zh: 对警务系统的全面彻底改造才能改变人们反应中的这种动态。

sentences.en: Of course, the problems police are facing today can't be solved by uniform change alone.
sentences.zh: 当然，警察今天面临的问题不能仅仅通过更换制服来解决。

sentences.en: But a change in uniform can be an important symbol, a way for police departments to signal to their communities that they want to have a better relationship.
sentences.zh: 但制服的改变可以是一个重要的象征，是警察局向社区发出信号表明他们希望建立更好关系的一种方式。

sentences.en: In the case of Chief Cizankas in Menlo Park, the uniform experiment did help lead to bigger changes.
sentences.zh: 就门洛帕克的西赞卡斯局长而言，制服实验确实有助于带来更大的改变。

sentences.en: Requiring officers to wear blazers meant a certain kind of officer was drawn to the police department.
sentences.zh: 要求警官穿西装外套意味着某种特定类型的警官会被吸引到警察局来。

sentences.en: The kind who was willing to get on board with the more significant reforms that Cizankas wanted to make.
sentences.zh: 那种愿意接受西赞卡斯想要做出的更重大改革的人。

sentences.en: And even though the department eventually abandoned the blazers, many of the other changes stuck.
sentences.zh: 尽管警局最终放弃了西装外套，但许多其他变革却保留了下来。

sentences.en: Here's former Menlo Park Assistant Chief Dominic Peloso again.
sentences.zh: 这位是前门洛帕克副局长多米尼克·佩洛索。

sentences.en: Vic was definitely ahead of his time.
sentences.zh: 维克绝对是个超越时代的人。

sentences.en: And, you know, as with most people who are ahead of their time, you don't have a crowd of people that all kind of stand up and cheer for you.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，就像大多数超越时代的人一样，你不会拥有一大群全都站起来为你欢呼的人。

sentences.en: But it would be very interesting because within, I'd say, 10 or 15 years, almost every police department in our area,
sentences.zh: 但非常有趣的是，我想在10到15年内，我们地区的几乎每一个警察局，

sentences.en: even though they didn't change the uniform or the titles or the organizational chart, were taking on that real big kind of community policing thing.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们没有改变制服、头衔或组织结构图，但都在采用那种非常宏大的社区警务模式。

sentences.en: They went ahead and did it because that was the signs of the times.
sentences.zh: 他们继续这样做了，因为那是时代的发展标志。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Delaney Hall with Katie Mingle, Sam Greenspan, Sharif Yousef, Kurt Colstead, Avery Truffleman, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 《99%无形》本周由德兰妮·霍尔与凯蒂·明格、萨姆·格林斯潘、谢里夫·优素福、库尔特·科尔斯特德、艾弗里·特鲁夫曼以及我罗曼·马斯共同制作。

sentences.en: Special thanks this week to Daryl Lindsey of the Menlo Park Police Department, Richard Johnson, Robert Mauro, David Cooper, and Tom DuPont.
sentences.zh: 本周特别鸣谢门洛帕克警察局的达里尔·林德西、理查德·约翰逊、罗伯特·毛罗、大卫·库珀和汤姆·杜邦。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 KALW in San Francisco and produced out of the offices of ArcSign, an architecture and interiors firm in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 KALW 的一个项目，制作于加利福尼亚州奥克兰市美丽市中心的建筑与室内设计公司 ArcSign 的办公室。

sentences.en: You can find the show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Facebook 上找到并关注这个节目。

sentences.en: You can follow us all on Twitter and Instagram.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Twitter 和 Instagram 上关注我们所有人。

sentences.en: But the best way to explore the 99% Invisible activity that shapes the design of our world is to click around the hundreds and hundreds of stories on 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 但探索塑造我们世界设计的《99%无形》活动的最好方法，是点击浏览 99pi.org 上的成百上千个故事。

sentences.zh: 伊迪托比亚。
